summary: Pierce County, WA: 40-ft L-6 pole tower dated 1947-48 near a 1942 house; removed 1963; 2016 visit found one leg and footings; private timberland, permit needed.

facts.design: 40' pole tower with L-6 cab; 8 x 8 ft cab with pyramid roof and two-foot catwalk
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1963 (firelookout.com says destroyed); 2016 visit found one leg on the ground and three nearly buried footings

access.note: Private timberland; Willhite says an expensive permit is required (2016 permit holder Hancock Forest Management)

visit.trail_note: Distance listed as drive-up on good gravel road; permit required on private timberland (Willhite, 2016)

events.note: First structure on the site was a house (Register); Willhite describes a 14 x 32 ft cabin built by the Aircraft Warning Service
Aircraft Warning Service station Jig 2-7 used existing state facilities at the site
40-ft pole tower with L-6 cab. Register and firelookout.com say 1948; the Forest Lookouts annual-report quote and Willhite say 1947
Tower removed (Register, Forest Lookouts, Willhite); firelookout.com says destroyed
Registered May 26, 2012; nominated by Ray Kresek
Willhite site visit: one tower leg on the ground, three nearly buried footings, at least one moved

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com give 1948; the Forest Lookouts quote of the 40th annual report and Willhite give 1947. The story reports both.
Register, Forest Lookouts and Willhite say removed; firelookout.com says destroyed. The year agrees across all four.
Register calls the 1942 first structure a house; Willhite calls a 14 x 32 ft cabin built by the Aircraft Warning Service. Both are reported as they are written.

notes_for_editor: Tower date conflicts between 1947 and 1948; story reports both. Brief access 'unknown' is better recorded as permission (Willhite, 2016). Brief registration event (2012) confirmed. Latest site report is 2016; no later source found. No photos taken from the Willhite gallery (licensing not checked).
